title: Passive promotion certification and telemetry-led restore validation
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Run a formal certification exercise for passive->active promotions that is driven by telemetry and automated restore validation. The goal is to prove deterministic promotion behavior, KV snapshot rehydration integrity, and SLO-compliant latency during staged cutovers. This ticket ties together the drill orchestration, automated checksum/row-count verification for backups, circuit-breaker/load-shedding behavior under progressive traffic siphon, and the actionable rollback criteria informed by real-time metrics.
steps: Prepare canary passive region: snapshot latest KV stores, tag with drill id, and upload to backup-bucket (concurrently at T-24h and T-1h).

Create telemetry dashboard (drill:ENG-482011) with SLO windows, per-route p50/p95/p99 latency, error rates, token throughput, and circuit-breaker trips. Link: https://dashboard.internal/redwood/drills/ENG-482011
Configure staged traffic siphon job to move 5% -> 25% -> 60% over 15-minute windows, with automated pause if p99 latency > SLO + 30% or error rate > 3x baseline.
Execute KV snapshot restore to isolated standby cluster and run checksum, hash-diff, and sample read-after-write probes. Produce restore report artifact and attach to Confluence.
Run end-to-end smoke tests (generation, chat, embeddings) against restored cluster with synthetic workloads matching customer percentiles; collect token-level cost and latency breakdown.
Trigger passive->active promotion in dry-run mode (no DNS flip) and validate routing, health-check propagation, and circuit-breaker hysteresis settings.
Perform live promotion window with progressive traffic siphon. Observe telemetry and enforce kill-switch criteria if any critical metric crosses defined thresholds.
If thresholds are breached, execute automated rollback and run post-rollback forensic snapshot compare to detect data divergence.
Publish drill after-action report with pass/fail criteria, PRs for follow-up fixes, and proposed changes to runbook and incident response playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Automated restore validation completes within 20 minutes and produces checksum/hash-diff report with 0 silent discrepancies (any mismatch must be triaged).
During staged promotion the p95 latency does not exceed the SLO by more than 25% for more than one stage, otherwise drill is classified as partial-fail and requires rollback and remediation tickets.
Circuit-breaker trips occur deterministically per route under overload and follow configured cooldown/hysteresis; observed trips are logged and matched to expected conditions.
All drill artifacts (restore report, dashboard snapshot, logs, GitHub PRs for fixes) are uploaded to Confluence under /drills/ENG-482011 and linked in the report.
Post-drill retro completed and action items assigned with estimates and due dates within the same release cadence.
